findings.description: The bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so objects (including the seeded vendor roster spreadsheet) are stored without enforced SSE-KMS/SSE-S3 default encryption. Unlike the audit_trail bucket, no KMS key is applied here.

findings.issue_category: no public access block or ACL
findings.description: This bucket declares neither an ACL nor an accompanying aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, so nothing prevents a later ACL or bucket policy from granting public read/write to the vendor data it stores. None of the buckets in this file have a public access block, but this one has no ACL restriction at all.
The ledger export bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so financial ledger data is stored without default encryption at rest.
Versioning and access logging are configured, but no default server-side encryption is defined, so model artifacts and any training data they embed are persisted unencrypted.

No server_side_encryption_configuration is set. Operational runbooks frequently contain hostnames, escalation procedures, and occasionally embedded credentials, and are stored here in cleartext at rest.

This bucket is the logging target for model_artifacts and holds audit records, yet force_destroy = true allows the entire log history to be deleted with a single terraform destroy, and there is no object lock or MFA delete to protect log integrity. Its ACL value 'lcatalogopts-delivery-write' is also not a valid canned ACL (apparently a corrupted 'log-delivery-write'), so the intended log-delivery grant is not reliably applied.

A vendor roster spreadsheet is uploaded with no kms_key_id or server_side_encryption argument into reports_archive, a bucket that also lacks default encryption, so this potentially sensitive third-party data lands in S3 entirely unencrypted.
